bull.b: The return to positive earnings and strong operating margins indicates that Protalix can currently convert product revenue into meaningful profit. If commercial sales remain durable, this improved earnings base should support internal funding, investment in the pipeline, and greater resilience over the next several quarters.

A debt-free balance sheet and substantial liquidity give Protalix flexibility to fund operations and advance clinical programs without immediate financing pressure. This reduces interest burden and preserves strategic options while the company develops commercial products and evaluates future pipeline needs.

Additional geographic approval and a less frequent dosing option can broaden Elfabrio’s commercial reach and improve its fit for patients and prescribers. Continued partner-led adoption could strengthen recurring product economics and support Protalix’s position in the Fabry disease market.

bear.b: Dependence on Chiesi purchasing patterns means reported revenue may not track underlying demand smoothly, making earnings and cash generation harder to forecast. Uneven shipments can also obscure the durability of commercial growth and increase reliance on partner execution over the next several quarters.

The milestone materially boosted first-half revenue but is not expected to recur in the same way, reducing comparability with future periods. Unless recurring Elfabrio sales replace that contribution, reported growth and profitability could moderate after the milestone-supported base rolls off.

The observed immunogenicity and unresolved regimen choice could complicate PRX-115’s development path, affecting trial design, timing, and eventual market positioning. These issues create execution risk for a pipeline asset that may otherwise provide an important future growth opportunity.
